post_letter_observations: NEW-13 (frozen): the letter says the noise SD was corrected to 0.06 on every dimension because the earlier '0.06-0.12' text 'does not hold for this policy'. This explanation exists only in the letter: the manuscript has no note of the correction, and the claim cannot be checked against code from the review inputs. If it is accurate, NEW-13 is a correction rather than a regression. The author should confirm it against the code and say so in App.B.

NEW-14 (frozen): the letter's R2 entry presents the general perception formula as complete but does not mention that App.B process step (6) still gives the inconsistent 'tau_i(p + b_i) + eta shrunk toward its trust target'.

NEW-16 (frozen): the letter's NEW-12 entry does not mention the new tab:secondary-cells caption, which repeats the 'after 2,000 rounds' wording for convergence time and omits the margins behind its '=' marker.

S2: the letter's statement that no model discounts a policy signal by trust exactly as PolicySwarm does is not a rebuttal of the positioning requirement. The audit can still be contrasted with trust as an opinion (Gestefeld & Lorenz) and trust as a driver of acceptance (Falcone & Sapienza).

NS-1 check: the letter does not falsely claim any of the six gaps listed by 2A (R12 five pilot cells, R13 dispersion-margin justification or all-rule CIs, S2 positioning, NEW-4 coding-invariant version, NEW-6 trust-row discussion, R5 Schweighofer tie). It leaves them unmentioned rather than misrepresenting them.
The letter's 'Corrections to the round-4 letter' section (R13, R11, R5) checks out against the manuscript and corrects the round-4 letter's overstatements in good faith.
The letter's anchor check ('Every anchor is checked by check_response.py') shows only that the anchors exist, not that the cited text meets the criteria.
